default: Could I get some ale, friend?
A tankard of your finest, if you please.
happy: This place has the best atmosphere!
impatient: How long does it take to pour ale?
Service is slower than usual today...

dismissed: This place used to be better.

default: A good fire and a full cup — can't ask for more.
This is the part of the day I look forward to.
Warm hearth, cold ale. Everything's where it should be.
Can't remember the last time I sat down all day.
My feet thank you. My purse, less so.
Heard there's work on the board. Not for me, mind.
Every tavern's got a story. This one's got an hourglass the size of a tree.
traveler: The road's long, but this ale makes it worth the miles.
Haven't sat by a fire this warm in weeks.
One more of these and I might just stay the night.
Three towns back they told me to stop here. They were right.
The bridge creaks, but it holds. So does this stool.
Mud on my boots from two counties. Don't mind it.
Nobody asks questions on the road. Nice to be asked for my order.
Rain followed me all the way from the pass.
I'll sleep in a hayloft tonight and dream of this ale.
local: Same seat, same ale. Some things you don't change.
Heard the miller's boy went off adventuring. Madness.
Nothing rounds off a long day like this.
My wife says I spend too much time here. She's not wrong.
The mill's been loud all week. This is the only quiet I get.
Old Maud swears the well water tastes of iron this year.
Harvest's coming in slow. Ale's coming in fine.
The guild lads were singing again last night. Out of tune, as always.
Grew up three doors down. Still the best seat in town.
soldier: Quiet night. I'll take quiet nights.
Off duty, and this cup's the only order I'll follow.
The keep can wait. This tankard can't.
Twelve hours at the gate. My feet have filed a complaint.
Captain says no drinking on duty. I'm not on duty.
Nothing crossed the bridge today but carts and gossip.
Polished the same helmet three times. Needed this.
If the horn sounds, I was never here.
Lord's orders, lord's wages. The ale's my own.
trader: Good day at market, better evening here.
I've drunk in richer towns. None friendlier.
A fair price and a full cup — that's a good day.
Sold wool to a man who swore he'd never buy wool. Drinks are on him.
The caravan's resting, and so am I.
Salt's up, iron's down, ale's just right.
I count coins all day. Let me count sips for once.
Word is the eastern pass is open again. Good for trade.
Every market has a best stall. Every town has a best tavern.

service_request: Been on the road since dawn — a drink would do wonders.
Long journey to get here. You got anything strong?
First warm place I've seen in two days. I'll take an ale.
Just passed the bridge. Any chance of a seat and a pint?
Road dust in my throat. Whatever you're pouring, I'll have it.
leaving: Back on the road tomorrow. This helped.
I'll remember this place when I'm back this way.

service_request: Same as usual, if you don't mind.
You know what I like. Don't make me ask.
Evening. The regular, please.
Good to be back. Rough day in the district.
Pour one for an old regular, would you?
Off duty. Don't try to sell me anything, just ale.
Long shift at the keep. I've earned this one.
Something to take the edge off. Whatever's cold.
Keep it quiet tonight, I just want a drink.
Ale. One. Maybe two.
leaving: Don't let this place get rowdy.

service_request: Docked the wagon an hour ago. First stop: here.
A drink to close out a good day on the market.
I've been haggling since sunrise. Ale. Now.
Seen three towns this week, and none with a decent tavern. You've got potential.
Merchant prices, merchant thirst. Pour generously.
leaving: I'll spread the word if the trade goes well.
Good enough to come back to.
Next caravan stops here. Count on it.
